title: The 10x Stock I'm Loading Up On This Month
creator: Asymmetric Investing
summary: In 'The 10x Stock I'm Loading Up On This Month' (published 2 Oct 2026), Travis Hoeft reveals his October buy for the Asymmetric (ACE Metro) portfolio: Zillow (Z), which he is buying as a 10x-over-10-years compounder despite the stock being down 61% over the past year. His four-part checklist — revenue growth, margin expansion, multiple expansion, buybacks — is, he argues, all present. Revenue is growing 17.7% and accelerating even in a weak housing market, driven by rentals ($734M TTM, +34% CAGR) and the mortgage leg rather than the traditional 8%-growth residential business; the company now positions itself as where people answer all housing questions, an aggregator that owns customer demand. Operating margin flipped from -13.5% (Mar-2024 quarter) to slightly positive, with $258M TTM free cash flow and ~$800M of recent buybacks shrinking shares from ~242M. Valuation looks unloved: ~11x forward P/E, ~15x forward P/FCF, 2.2x sales. His main criticism is stock-based compensation (still $363M, down from $423M) and he admits the housing market could get worse short-term, but sees that as the launching pad. Note: this is a cross-creator divergence — Joseph Hogue had Z as AVOID on 30 Sep on housing-supply-chain weakness. Call: Z BUY.

calls.stated_price: No explicit target; ~11x forward P/E, ~15x forward P/FCF (24x trailing), 2.2x sales; stock down 61% over the past year
calls.thesis: October buy for the Asymmetric portfolio: Zillow is the aggregator of US housing demand (residential + mortgage + rentals). Revenue growth 17.7% and accelerating; rentals segment $734M TTM at +34% CAGR; op margin flipped from -13.5% to positive; FCF $258M TTM; ~$800M of buybacks, net cash on balance sheet. Expects market outperformance over 5-10 years.
calls.base_case: Accelerating growth + margin expansion + multiple expansion as the market re-rates a profitable compounder.
calls.bull_case: Multi-trillion-dollar housing market network effect compounds; buybacks retire meaningful share count at depressed multiples.
calls.bear_case: Stock-based comp still too high ($363M, down from $423M); housing transaction volumes could worsen with mortgage rates elevated; FCF lumpy.
